title: Gov. Matt Meyer signs legislation to help fire companies in Delaware - NewsBreak
text:
8 hours ago
WILMINGTON— Support is coming for Delaware fire companies and those who serve their respective communities.
Gov. Matt Meyer signed several bills Aug. 9 that will provide additional support to firemen and their family members — efforts that have been long in the works.
“Volunteer firefighters save lives every day,” Gov. Meyer said in statement.
“As state leaders, it is critical that we create meaningful incentives to bring new volunteers into these essential roles and honor those who serve. These bills are an investment in public safety, in teaching the next generation, and in the dedicated Delawareans who answer the call when we need them most.”
Of the legislation, House Bill 171, sponsored by Rep. Debra Heffernan, D-Bellefonte, would update the Delaware Volunteerism Act to clarify that high school students can complete community service requirements with local fire departments.
That service would equate to one elective credit for high school students, and would require schools to let students know that this opportunity is available to them.
The other bill, Senate Bill 28, sponsored by Sen. Darius Brown, D-Wilmington, updates burial benefit laws for volunteer firefighters.
The now-law requires that $7,000 in funeral expenses is owed to volunteer firefighters, volunteer fire company ladies auxiliary and volunteer ambulance and rescue members. It will apply to members who have served as state employees and will take effect on Oct. 1.
“Volunteer firefighters are not just heroes; they are members of our communities, our friends, and our family,” Sen. Brown said.
“When a tragedy strikes, the last thing their loved ones should have to worry about is financial stress during an already painful time. By receiving the fixed benefit of $7,000, we can show our appreciation and commitment to supporting them and their families — both in life and in death.”
The additional bills signed by Gov. Meyer were Senate Bill 86 and House Bill 124. The former was sponsored by Sen. Russ Huxtable, D-Lewes, and the latter by Rep. Kim Williams, D-Newport.
The first of those would allow donations and additional funds for the Delaware Volunteer Fire Service Revolving Loan Fun, and the second would increase maximum amount of fees that the state Fire Marshal’s Office.
Those fees include bringing portable unit fire suppression appliances from $50 to $100 and increasing fees for all other permits, licenses and certifications from $25 to $100.
